earlier_scan.note: Glottolog refs are only ethnography (Norstrom 2003) and a subclassification survey (Varghese & Mathew 2015); no grammar/phonology of Paliyan found.

sources.citation: SPPEL (Scheme for Protection and Preservation of Endangered Languages, CIIL Mysuru) website, Southern zone / Kerala list: 'PALIYA' listed as a target language.
sources.note: No grammatical sketch, dictionary or feature database published for Paliya as of 2026-09-17 (only Luro, Sanenyo, Eravalla sketches exist).

Tamil University publication no. 205. Thanjavur: Tamil University. ISBN 81-7090-265-7. Section 4.8 'பழியர் கிளைமொழி (தமிழ்)' [Paliyar dialect (Tamil)], pp. 178-179.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The 'ஒலியனியல்' (phonology) paragraph, explicitly summarising Muralidharan (1985), gives only the inventory: 10 vowel phonemes (i, i:, e, e:, a, a:, u, u:, o, o:) and 16 consonant phonemes, /j/ only in loans (ji:ppu 'jeep'); then pronouns, 8 cases, tense suffixes. States the Paliyar speech is a dialect of Tamil showing no large linguistic differences from neighbouring speech. No word on stress/accent (அழுத்தம்).

sources.citation: Menon, T. Madhava (chief ed.). 1996. The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, Vol. II. Thiruvananthapuram: International School of Dravidian Linguistics. Entries 'PALIYAN' (M. Sasikumar) and 'MALA PULAYA'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Paliyan entry: 'The Paliya in Kerala speak a corrupted dialect of Tamil with many Malayalam words and usages.' Mala Pulaya entry: 'They speak a dialect of Tamil which is unintelligible to Tamil speakers'. Unlike many other tribes in the volume there is no 'PALIYAN LANGUAGE' or 'MALA PULAYA LANGUAGE' entry, i.e. ISDL had no linguistic sketch to draw on.
